Golden-pink rays crack through cumulus clouds, striking her upturned cheek as she squints softly skyward, peach warmth pooling across her collarbone.
Orange-pumpkin sky deepens behind the water tower; she tilts her head sideways, watching the gradient shift with quiet fascination.
First neon signs flicker on across the avenue below, blue-pink pulse catching the gloss of her eyes as she glances toward them.
Sun-disc hangs fat and amber just above the skyline; she raises her palm flat, measuring its width against distant rooftops with a gentle smile.
Flock of starlings sweeps through the midground in a murmuration ribbon; she tracks them left, chin lifted, lips parting slightly in surprise.
Billboard lights up suddenly behind the neighboring building; she notices the glow shift on her hands and looks over with curious amusement.
First raindrops bloom dark on the rooftop concrete beside her sneakers; she crouches, touching one wet circle with a fingertip.
Cherry petals lift from the courtyard below in a slow spiral; she reaches out sideways, letting two settle briefly on her open wrist.
Streetlamp cascade activates block by block into the distance; she leans on the railing, chin on forearm, counting each new amber dot.
Distant lightning flashes white behind storm clouds at the far horizon; she freezes mid-sentence, eyes wide, watching the brief branching light.
Passing jet draws a clean contrail across the deepening violet sky; she follows it slowly with her gaze, expression softening into something wistful.
Golden hour melts into blue hour mid-moment, the warm tone on her face shifting cool; she blinks, noticing the change on her own skin.
Sudden mist rolls in from the east, softening the city edges; she wraps both arms around herself and turns her face toward the veil.
Hot-air balloon drifts silently overhead in peach and ivory stripes; she spots it first, pointing upward with one finger, mouth open in delight.
Temple bell tolls three times from the valley below; she goes still, eyes closing briefly, letting the resonance settle around her shoulders.
Heat lightning pulses orange-white behind downtown towers; she leans forward on both palms, studying the irregular rhythm with narrowed, intent eyes.
Autumn leaves cyclone upward from the alley below into the rooftop frame; she laughs, ducking her head as one brushes past her ear.
Fireflies begin emerging at the rooftop garden edge in soft drifting sparks; she kneels beside the planter box, watching one hover near her knee.
Festival firework bursts gold above the far district; she flinches at the crack then smiles wide, the bloom reflected as twin points in her eyes.
Figure on the opposite rooftop waves broadly; she spots them, straightens, and waves back with both arms raised above her head.
Moth circles the single rooftop lantern in slow velvet loops; she tilts her face toward it, watching each orbit with unhurried, gentle attention.
First stars appear in the deep indigo gap between clouds; she tips her chin up, lips moving faintly as if counting or naming them.
Blowing confetti from a party below drifts into the rooftop midground in pink and gold flecks; she catches one piece and reads whatever is printed.
Dragonfly hovers perfectly still at eye level near the ledge; she holds her breath and goes motionless, studying its translucent wings against the orange sky.
Sun-disc finally touches the roofline and the sky ignites coral-gold; she shields her eyes with the flat of one hand and exhales slowly.
